bus.name: Gies College of Business
bus.who: First-year University of Illinois students currently enrolled in another program who want a Gies Business degree. Sophomores are not eligible; the page's FAQ covers that case.
eligibility: Be a first-year current student at Illinois.
Have completed at least 24 graded credit hours at Illinois by the end of the first spring semester.
Follow the course completion timelines below.
bus.requiredBy: the end of your first spring semester

required.label: At least one of MATH 115, MATH 220, MATH 221, MATH 231, MATH 234 or STAT 100

dataScienceExtra.label: One of MATH 234 (recommended), MATH 220 or MATH 221

recommended: Levels I to III of a language other than English; priority goes to students who have completed three levels or passed a proficiency exam, and high school coursework counts.
CS 105 Intro Computing: Non-Tech (all majors except + Data Science)
notes: The application is competitive: a major choice, essay prompts and additional considerations.
Gies undergraduate programs must be completed in no more than 9 full-time semesters.
The Fall 2026 application deadline was May 20, 2026; Fall 2027 deadlines will be posted by January 2027.
Transferring can change tuition rate, scholarship eligibility, course loads, dual-degree and study-abroad plans; the college asks students to talk to their current advisor first.

engineering-undeclared.name: The Grainger College of Engineering
engineering-undeclared.who: Current Illinois students who entered the university as first-year students, in their second and/or third semester. Every intercollegiate transfer student enters Grainger through Engineering Undeclared, not directly in a major.
engineering-undeclared.notEligible: Fourth-semester students, juniors, seniors, and transfer students are not eligible to ICT into EU.
engineering-undeclared.transferEntry: If you entered the university as a transfer student in a major outside of Grainger Engineering you are not eligible to apply. Off-campus transfer students must be admitted directly to Grainger Engineering at time of transfer.
eligibility: Entered Illinois as a first-year student; apply in the second and/or third semester.
Minimum specialized GPA (the Grainger Engineering GPA) of 3.0 or higher, with a B- or better in individual technical courses.

required.label: General Chemistry 1 (CHEM 102 and 103). CHEM 103 is waived when CHEM 102 credit came from an AP, IB or A-level exam (some majors may still require it), not when it came from a proficiency exam.

competitive.text: The application asks for three majors of interest in ranked preference, and only two may be competitive majors. Indicating more than two competitive majors will have a negative impact on an application.

closedMajors.text: Computer Science, Computer Science + Bioengineering and Computer Science + Physics are closed to on-campus transfer, including Engineering Undeclared; they are direct-admission only.
offers: The Siebel School says many other majors, including some blended CS + X majors, are available for transfer once students are admitted, and that each department and college has its own requirements, so consult your academic advisor.

The CS minor: nearly all Illinois degrees can be paired with it (CS, CS + X and Computer Engineering majors cannot). It gives no registration advantage in CS courses, takes a minimum of four semesters, and should be begun no later than the first semester of junior year.

recommended: After Calculus 1 and General Chemistry 1, the page suggests more technical/STEM courses that count toward your majors of interest, commonly math and physics, and says to take technical courses at Illinois if the required ones came from AP, IB, A-level or transfer credit.

The page's informal guide to courses Grainger students take that non-EU students can take: MATH 231, MATH 241, MATH 257 and MATH 285 (Engineering Mechanics takes MATH 441 instead of MATH 285); PHYS 211 and PHYS 212; CHEM 104 and 105, required for Agricultural and Biological, Bio-, Chemical, Civil and Environmental Engineering, Engineering Mechanics and Materials Science & Engineering, and one option for Mechanical Engineering's science elective.
CS 101 is required for all majors except Computer Engineering and Electrical Engineering.

TAM 211 is listed for Aerospace, Agricultural & Biological, Civil, Environmental, Industrial, Mechanical, and Nuclear, Plasma, and Radiological Engineering, Engineering Mechanics, and Systems Engineering & Design. Aerospace, Mechanical and Nuclear, Plasma, and Radiological Engineering require TAM 210 but accept TAM 211 in its place; majors that require TAM 211 do not accept TAM 210. From Spring 2026 non-Grainger students add their name to a waitlist for TAM 211.

MCB 150 is required for Agricultural & Biological Engineering, Bioengineering, the Materials Science & Engineering Biomaterials track and Neural Engineering, and can count as a science elective for Mechanical Engineering.
notes: Admission is competitive: EU accepts a limited number of ICT students each semester.

Applications must be submitted by 11:59 PM on the last day of the window, and a window may be moved so it does not close on a weekend or holiday. The page says: "The Fall 2026 application will be open November 15 - November 30, 2026."

The application asks for three majors of interest in ranked order, a resume, an academic record essay, an extracurricular involvement essay, a professional statement of interest and an optional essay about extenuating circumstances.
Start with an ICT information session; they are held every fall and spring semester, virtually and in person.
EU advisors are not able to course plan for students who are not yet in the program; the page says to consult your own academic advisor about course selections.

From the EU program page: students who transfer in their second or third semester enter Grainger in their third or fourth, stay in EU at least one semester, and transfer into a major by the start of their fifth semester.
The page lists Calculus 1 and General Chemistry 1 as the course requirements for ICT to EU without saying whether they must be finished before the window opens.

engineering.name: The Grainger College of Engineering
engineering.path: Transfer admission (the college's published transfer coursework)
engineering.who: Students transferring to Illinois from another school. The page says a transfer student who wants a Grainger major must apply and be admitted directly into the college at the time of transfer, and that transfer students admitted to other colleges on campus are not eligible for later admission or intercollegiate transfer (ICT) to Engineering Undeclared or Grainger. Current Illinois students who entered as first-year students apply through Engineering Undeclared instead.
eligibility: The college generally expects a minimum 3.00 overall GPA; admission to specific majors can be much more competitive, and the average admitted transfer GPA is above 3.50.
B or better (3.00 to 4.00) in all prerequisite courses, taken in the terms the major's suggested sequence expects, with three to four technical courses and 15 or more credit hours each semester.

required.label: CHEM 102 and CHEM 103 General Chemistry I
CHEM 104 and CHEM 105 General Chemistry II (see the page's footnote)
MATH 220 Calculus or MATH 221 Calculus I
PHYS 212 University Physics: Electricity and Magnetism
One or more of CS 101, CS 124, CS 125, ECE 110, MATH 227, MATH 257, MCB 150, STAT 107, SE 101 or ME 170, as the major's Transfer Handbook recommends

notes: Transfer applications open January 15 for fall entry; see the page for the current deadline.
